Artificial turf cleaning service in Kissimmee, Florida

An artificial turf cleaning service rinses, power brooms and deodorizes turf so it drains, smells and looks the way it did on installation day. In Kissimmee, a basic visit runs roughly $80 to $150 and a deep clean with pet-odor treatment runs $150 to $400, based on published 2026 market ranges. Central Florida's oak leaf drop, pollen and lovebug seasons all shape the schedule.

Reviewed by Luis Austin, owner · Last reviewed September 21, 2026

What maintenance does artificial turf need?

Artificial turf needs a hose rinse every week or two, power brooming a few times a year to lift matted pile, and a deeper sanitizing clean twice a year timed around Central Florida's live oak leaf drop and rainy season. Storms and heavy pollen weeks call for an extra pass in between. None of it involves an in-ground sprinkler; the state synthetic turf rule doesn't allow one to water turf at all.

Artificial turf maintenance calendar for Central Florida
FrequencyTaskWhy it matters here
Weekly (pet yards), every other week otherwiseHose rinse and a quick debris checkCentral Florida heat turns urine into odor fast; Rule 62-308.100 bars using an in-ground irrigation system on turf, so every rinse here is by hose
MonthlyPower broom against the grain, check infill depthRegular traffic and lovebug season, roughly April–May and again August–September in Florida, mat the pile down and leave residue that needs brushing out
Twice a year, spring and fallDeep clean: sanitizing rinse, infill top-up, edge and seam checkTimed around the live oak leaf drop in late winter into early spring and just ahead of the June–September rainy season
After named storms or heavy pollen weeksRake off debris, rinse the pollen film, check for standing waterAfternoon storms can drop one to three inches an hour; spring pollen coats turf in a yellow film a plain rinse lifts

How often should pet turf be cleaned?

Dog turf needs a hose rinse most days at the spot a dog actually uses, and at least once a week across the whole run, because Central Florida heat turns bacteria in urine into odor within hours. Beyond that, plan on a professional deep clean with an enzyme or antimicrobial treatment every three to four months, sooner with more than one dog or a yard that stays shaded and damp.

Pet turf systems built with a fully permeable backing and zeolite or an antimicrobial-coated sand hold up longer between professional visits than regular lawn turf pressed into service as a dog run. This guide covers what to try if odor has already set in.

Who needs a professional visit, and who just needs a hose

An artificial turf cleaning service covers pet odor removal, turf deodorizing, power brooming, an infill top-up, turf sanitizing, and an enzyme cleaner worked into the backing where plain water doesn't reach. A homeowner's own rinse-and-broom routine covers most yards for the first year or two: hose it down, brush the high-traffic path, blow off leaves before they break down into the infill. A professional visit earns its cost once infill has visibly thinned, pet odor survives a normal rinse, or the pile in a traffic lane has matted down and stopped standing back up on its own.

Vacation rentals are the other common case: a cleaning pass between a heavy booking stretch keeps the yard looking like the listing photos without the owner managing it long-distance. It's not worth booking a professional clean for turf under a year old with no pets and no visible problem; that money is better spent on nothing at all until there's something to actually fix.

What a cleaning visit actually does

Here's the sequence on a standard visit, start to finish.

  1. Walk the yard first. Check for matting, staining, low spots holding water, and any seam or edge that needs a separate repair call before cleaning goes ahead of it.
  2. Clear debris before water touches it. Leaves, acorns and lovebug residue get raked or blown off dry; wetting them first just presses them into the infill.
  3. Power broom against the grain. Lifts flattened pile and works old, compacted infill loose so it can be topped up evenly instead of layered over.
  4. Treat odor at the source. An enzyme or antimicrobial solution goes down into the infill and backing, not just across the top of the blades.
  5. Top up infill to depth. Brought back to roughly the original one to two pounds per square foot rather than left thin where it's washed or blown away.
  6. Final hose rinse and brush. A steady hose, not a high-pressure wand aimed to blast a section clean, which can strip infill and fray blade tips.

What turf cleaning costs

Published 2026 market ranges put a basic maintenance visit, rinse, debris removal and a power brooming, at $80 to $150 (a national cleaning-cost survey). A standard deep clean with infill work runs $150 to $400, and most homes land between $200 and $350. Pet-odor and sanitizing treatments sit toward the top of that range, because the enzyme product and the labor to work it into the infill cost more than a plain rinse.

Heat, pollen and lovebugs: cleaning turf through a Central Florida year

Heat is why pet odor here needs more attention than the same yard would in a cooler climate; warmth speeds up the bacteria that turn urine into smell, so a rinse schedule that works up north isn't enough in Kissimmee. Live oaks drop their old leaves as new growth comes in, typically late winter into early spring (UF/IFAS live oak information), and the tannins in a pile of wet oak leaves can stain turf fiber if they sit through a few afternoon storms. Florida runs two lovebug swarms a year, spring and again in late summer (UF/IFAS Extension on lovebugs), and their residue is acidic enough to dull turf color if it bakes in the sun instead of getting rinsed off within a day or two.

Rainy season, June through September, does some of the cleaning for free by washing dust and pollen off the blades, but it also carries loose debris into low spots where Kissimmee's sandy base has settled, so those spots need an extra pass after a heavy storm.

Does cleaning affect drainage rules?

Florida's synthetic turf standard requires an installed lawn to stay permeable and not increase runoff onto a neighbor's property (a summary of the state standard). Infill packed solid with years of dust, pollen and pet waste can slow how fast water actually gets through the backing, even though the product itself is still rated for the same drainage. Regular power brooming and an infill top-up are what keep the real-world drainage close to the rated manufacturer specification of more than 30 inches an hour, which matters most on lots near a pond or swale, where the state standard already limits how close turf can sit to the water.

What a rushed cleaning job misses

A pressure washer aimed at the turf instead of a hose is the most common shortcut, and it can blow infill out of a section, fray blade tips, and on an older lawn loosen a seam that a gentler rinse would have left alone. Skipping the debris pass and going straight to water just presses leaves and lovebug residue deeper into the pile instead of removing them.

Spraying a deodorizer on top of the blades without working it into the infill treats the smell for a few days and misses where the odor actually comes from. And a clean that skips the infill top-up leaves the backing exposed in traffic lanes, which shows up as a dull, thin-looking stripe within a season.

Between visits

Rinse pet areas with a hose a few times a week between professional visits, more often at the peak of a Florida summer. Brush high-traffic paths against the grain every month or two so the pile keeps standing up on its own. Rake or blow off leaves and lovebug residue within a day or two rather than letting an afternoon storm work them into the infill. This guide covers debris season in more detail. If a spot keeps re-staining or smelling no matter how often it's rinsed, that's usually a sign for a repair visit rather than another cleaning.

How do you find the best turf cleaning company near me?

Ask what's actually included: a rinse and a broom is not the same service as an enzyme treatment worked into the infill, and the price should say which one you're getting. Ask whether infill gets topped up as part of the visit or billed separately, since a clean that leaves infill thin looks worse within weeks. And ask how they handle water pressure; a company that can't explain why it uses a hose instead of a pressure washer probably hasn't thought about what a blast of water does to years-old backing.

Tell us the yard size, whether pets use it, and when it was last cleaned, and we'll quote the visit.

Questions people ask

How long after a cleaning visit can pets or kids use the yard again?

Usually right away for a basic rinse and broom. If an enzyme or sanitizing treatment was applied, give it fifteen to twenty minutes to sit before heavy use, and a bit longer in shade where things dry more slowly.

Does turf cleaning remove old pet odor completely?

Often, if the odor is in the infill and hasn't reached the backing or the base underneath. Odor that survives a proper deep clean and a fresh infill swap usually means urine has worked past the infill, which points toward replacement rather than another cleaning.

Can I clean artificial turf myself between professional visits?

Yes, and it's the better routine. A hose rinse, a stiff push broom used against the grain, and prompt removal of leaves and debris cover most of what turf needs between the twice-yearly deep cleans.

What's the difference between power brooming and brushing?

Power brooming uses a machine, usually a walk-behind unit with rotating bristles, to lift matted pile and loosen packed infill across a large area quickly. Hand brushing with a stiff broom does the same job on a smaller scale or in tight corners a machine can't reach.

Do you top up infill during a regular cleaning visit?

Yes, when it's visibly thin. Infill migrates and compacts over time from rinsing, rain and foot traffic, and a clean that only rinses and broomes without restoring the depth leaves the backing more exposed than before.

How soon after a storm should turf be cleaned?

Within a few days if debris or standing water is visible. Leaves and organic matter left wet against the blades start to break down and stain the fiber faster in Florida heat than they would in a cooler climate.

Will cleaning turf void a warranty from the original installer?

A hose rinse and gentle power brooming shouldn't affect a manufacturer's warranty; those cover UV fade and material defects, not maintenance. A pressure washer or harsh chemical could, so ask the original installer what the warranty language actually excludes before using either.
